thread:
maria: Heads-up — the canary traffic shift job was blocked by the env-checker. policy checksum mismatch between staging and prod for `networkpolicy` + canary pods are landing without `nvidia` nodeSelector (so they fall back to cpu nodes).

deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused: preflight policy-check failed (exit=1). Details: networkpolicy.sha != git:networkpolicy.sha, pod.spec.nodeSelector mismatch.

kai: any recent chart/helm-value churn that touches networkpolicy or nodeSelector? :eyes:

maria: Not in prod. Staging got a chart bump earlier today from #deploys — looks like a templating change removed the `nodeSelector` default. Quick diff i ran: 
```
# from staging cluster
kubectl -n infra get networkpolicy default-allow -o yaml | sha256sum
# => e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855

# from git (main)
git show origin/main:charts/platform/templates/networkpolicy.yaml | sha256sum
# => 6d7fce9fee471194aa8b5b6e47267f03ab5e9b3b541a5c3e6e8f5a6c3d4f7e1a
```

ben: that sha diff looks legit. also saw a helm hook in the new chart that strips annotations for pod templates — maybe the nodeSelector default got moved into an annotation and then removed by our chart-processing admission.

ash: typo: "ash" here — we ran `helm template` locally and the generated manifest had `nodeSelector: {}` because the default value got overridden by a blank value in staging-values.yaml. i.e. staging-values had `gpu.nodeSelector: ""` by mistake.

kai: ok — so root cause: values override in staging -> empty value -> manifests diverge -> policy-check fails. but why did canary-run try to shift traffic before this was caught earlier? the preflight should have compared git->cluster earlier in pipeline.

sre-bot: Auto-alert: env-diff check failed for service=canary, rule=policy-parity, severity=high. Ticket created: INF-7321.

maria: pipeline did run parity check but our `helm-diff` step only compares rendered manifests vs last-deployed, not against git main. the new policy-check step was a late add and only runs on merge, not on canary-trigger. need to make it consistent.

ben: short-term fix: patch staging to restore gpu.nodeSelector from git so canary can test on gpu nodes. i'll push a hotfix PR to staging values with the correct selector.

ash: steps to reconcile (quick):
```bash
# restore nodeSelector in staging via gitops
gh pr create --title "fix: restore gpu.nodeSelector in staging-values" --body "restore default nodeSelector to avoid canary landing on cpu nodes"
# once merged
gitopsctl reconcile --repo infra-config --env staging --wait
# force re-run preflight
deploy-bot trigger preflight --env staging --pipeline canary-check
```

kai: also add a parity rule: compare rendered manifests in pipeline to `origin/main` rendered manifests and fail fast. I can file a small RFC.

maria: agree. action items: ben -> PR and hotfix; kai -> RFC for rendered-manifest parity in canary pipeline; ash -> add murmur test to smoke script to ensure canary pods see GPU nodes. i'll monitor INF-7321 and will re-run canary after reconcile.

ben: PR up: #2387. patch applied to staging-values. awaiting merge. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: GitOps sync detected new commit, reconcile job started for env=staging.

maria: after sync i'll run the smoke: `/smoke canary gpu-check` and post results here. if green, we'll re-run the traffic shift.

kai: long-term: add a lint rule in our chart CI to reject empty-string overrides for structural values (nodeSelector, tolerations). i'll attach a proposal to the RFC.

maria: thanks team. tagging @kai @ben @ash. will follow up with postmortem if the hotfix doesn't stabilize. :pray:
